title: Learning from Next-Frame Prediction: Towards Unified and Scalable Visual World Modeling
abstract: arXiv:2610.30724v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Video provides a natural source of supervision: what happens next serves as a learning signal for visual world modeling. Yet masked video pretraining focuses on recovering missing content from surrounding context rather than predicting the future from the past. Autoregressive methods instead predict forward one token at a time, but have yet to match joint-embedding methods in representation quality. This gap motivates us to revisit the granularity and space of future prediction. In this work, we introduce VANE, a self-supervised visual pretraining framework built on next-frame prediction in embedding space. A causal encoder summarizes past observations for a state predictor that infers the representation of the entire next frame, making temporal evolution the primary learning signal. This prediction is carried out in a fixed embedding space provided by a frozen semantic tokenizer, emphasizing scene content and structure. To ret

translated_title: 从下一帧预测中学习：迈向统一且可扩展的视觉世界建模
translated_abstract: 视频提供了一种天然的监督来源：接下来发生的事情可以作为视觉世界建模的学习信号。然而，掩码视频预训练侧重于从周围上下文中恢复缺失内容，而非根据过去预测未来。自回归方法则逐个token向前预测，但在表示质量上尚未能媲美联合嵌入方法。这一差距促使我们重新审视未来预测的粒度与空间。在这项工作中，我们提出了VANE，一个建立在嵌入空间中下一帧预测之上的自监督视觉预训练框架。因果编码器总结过去的观测信息，供状态预测器推断整个下一帧的表示，使时间演化成为主要的学习信号。该预测在一个由冻结的语义分词器提供的固定嵌入空间中进行，强调场景内容与结构。
tldr: 提出VANE自监督视觉预训练框架，通过在冻结语义分词器提供的固定嵌入空间中预测整个下一帧的表示，将时间演化作为核心学习信号，实现统一且可扩展的视觉世界建模。
